subject: maths
title: Ratio — simplify and share

slides.heading: Ratio — comparing quantities as parts
slides.body: A ratio compares two or more quantities by describing how many parts each has. The ratio 5:3 means for every 5 parts of the first quantity there are 3 of the second. Ratios can be simplified by dividing all parts by their highest common factor (HCF), and used to share a total — by finding the value of one part first, then multiplying.
slides.note: Maximum 3 sentences. Plain English. No AQA references. What is this and why does it matter.

slides.heading: Simplifying and sharing in ratio
slides.formula: Simplify: divide all parts by HCF | Share: one part = total ÷ (sum of ratio parts)
slides.formulaExplained: To simplify a ratio, find the highest common factor of all the numbers and divide every part by it — the ratio 30 : 18 simplifies to 5 : 3 (HCF = 6). To share a total in a given ratio: add all the ratio numbers to find the total number of parts; divide the total quantity by this to find one part; then multiply one part by each ratio number to find each share. Always check: the shares must add back to the original total.
slides.whenToUse: Any time you need to write a ratio in its simplest form, or share a quantity (money, ingredients, length) between people or groups in a given ratio.
slides.note: Show formula in standard notation. Explain each variable. State when this formula applies.

slides.heading: Let's work through one
slides.question: Share £108 in the ratio 5 : 4.

steps.instruction: Find the total number of parts by adding the ratio numbers.
Find the value of one part.
Multiply one part by each ratio number to find both shares.
Check the shares add back to the original total.

slides.note: Numbers must differ from any question in the question bank for this subtopic.

slides.heading: Watch out for this

mistakes.mistake: Dividing the total by the largest ratio number instead of the sum — e.g. for £108 in ratio 5:4, dividing by 5 to get £21.60 per part instead of dividing by 9 to get £12.
mistakes.correction: Always divide by the sum of all ratio parts, not just one of them. For 5:4, the total is 5+4=9 parts.

mistakes.mistake: Dividing by a common factor that is not the HCF when simplifying, then stopping — e.g. simplifying 30:18 by dividing by 3 to get 10:6, then treating 10:6 as fully simplified.
mistakes.correction: Keep simplifying until no common factor remains. 10:6 still has HCF 2 → 5:3. Or find the HCF (6) at the start and divide in one step: 30÷6 : 18÷6 = 5:3.

mistakes.mistake: When the difference between shares is given, dividing by the total parts instead of the difference in parts — e.g. if one person gets £56 more than another in ratio 5:3, dividing £56 by 8 (total parts) instead of by 2 (the difference 5−3).
mistakes.correction: If a difference between shares is given: find the difference in ratio parts (5−3=2), then 1 part = difference in value ÷ 2, then scale up for each share.

slides.note: Minimum 2, maximum 3 mistakes. Specific not generic.

keyFacts.fact: To simplify a ratio, divide all parts by their HCF in one step. The ratio 30:18 has HCF 6, giving 5:3.
keyFacts.examTip: If your simplified ratio still has a common factor, you haven't found the true HCF. Check by trying 2, 3, 5 as factors.

keyFacts.fact: To share in ratio: find total parts (add all ratio numbers), then 1 part = total quantity ÷ total parts, then multiply each ratio number by 1 part.
keyFacts.examTip: Check: all the shares must add back to the original total. If they don't, you divided by the wrong number.

keyFacts.fact: If the difference between two shares is known, the difference in ratio parts is the key: 1 part = difference in value ÷ difference in ratio parts.
keyFacts.examTip: For ratio a:b with difference d: 1 part = d ÷ (a−b). This is a different method from the standard sharing approach.
